Fourteen of verify-baseline's twenty-six keys read ZERO, and a counter held
at zero is not a measurement — it is a proof nobody minted. The medium
already holds proofs directly and says so in its own words: diag_refuses,
"born at ZERO on every program measured, which is the point: it does not
police a mistake, it holds an invariant."

T_UseAfterMove goes first because its arming condition was stated in the
artifact and already met — the fixture's own comment said "narration until
the wheel's own census reaches 0 (the arming law)", and the census reached 0
at the Phase 4.1 landing and held every board since. It is EUseAfterMove
now: SError, a diag_refuses arm, the frontier leg re-banked from
run_narration to a refusal contract and seen RED first (exit 0, 4,474 WAT
bytes against the unarmed tree). use_after_move_max RETIRES — an armed class
has nothing to count, because a wheel carrying one cannot compile, and a
landing that arms while keeping the key has kept the proxy beside the proof.

Two assumptions died measuring it, both mine: the T_/E_ prefix is not a
severity encoding (ERedundantBraces is E_ and SWarning; T_ marks membership
in SYNTAX's narration table), and diag_refuses is not the whole arming —
pipeline gates on diag_severity == SError first, so a warning never reaches
the refusal question.

mentl/cce356d:
The banked probe ran and killed itself first. It asked whether a
definition was renamed while a caller kept the old symbol. It was not:
both generations define both naming forms, and the annotation shifts
exactly one fn from bare to qualified — m2 carries two digit* definitions
and one parse_int_digit*, m3 the mirror. The earlier defs=0 was an
artifact of a trailing-space pattern. Fifth explanation this arc has
killed by measuring rather than reasoning.

Then the instrument changed kind, and that is what answered. Reading the
WAT had reached its limit, so the artifact was run: m3.wasm fed the
wheel's own source, 2645362 bytes in and zero out at exit 134,
reproduces the failure by hand with a backtrace. `wasm trap: indirect
call type mismatch`, innermost frame parse_int_go, reached through
lex_from, lex, infer_program_converged, compile_stdin_run.

So the fault is indirect dispatch at the renamed nested fn — not rows,
not symbols, not readers. A nested function's name is reaching its
call_indirect identity, which is the emitter's known hazard family with a
new trigger: a rename changing which definition an indirect call
resolves to.

The arc is now three steps. The indirect-dispatch fault sits upstream of
the discriminator fix, which sits upstream of the writer flip. Nothing
about the row tail can land until a nested fn can be renamed without
breaking dispatch, and that ordering was invisible until the artifact was
run instead of read.

Next probe is the prescribed one: wasm-objdump at the trapping address,
reading the call_indirect and the type it expected against the type it
got.

Boot unchanged; docs only.

mentl/cc487f8:
An 8-agent adversarial audit overturned the destiny-audit framing that
names-are-handles (R1) clears the 594 self-compile false effect-mismatches.
Measured: ~80% were an unresolved-row-var class dying at row_subsumes'
`EfClosed-gate vs EfOpen-body => _ => false` arm, and the shared root is
pointer-eq at the membership leaf. name_set_contains_loop compared
`list_index(set, i) == name`, which floors to i32.eq because the untyped
list erases the element to a word — so two byte-equal ENamed("Memory")
minted at distinct sites never merged, breaking set-dedup (422/598 rows
carried duplicate names) so the open tail never closed.

The leaf now matches BY NAME (str_eq on eff_name_str), exactly as the
negation gate already did (name_in_forbidden). row_subsumes resolves both
inputs first — a bound tail surfaces so a hidden forbidden effect is still
checked — and mirrors the EfOpen-gate arm for an open body against a closed
gate: the free tail is empty after inference for a monomorphic fn, and the
existing call-site rebind closes it to the declared row.

string_in_list (own.mn's ref-escape check over a list of Strings) is
un-conflated from name_set_contains, which it aliased — by-name deref
traps on a bare String; the two are different element types and get
different comparisons.

Measured: false mismatches 598 -> 146 (76%); crown 5/5, 66/66 micros, all
CLI verbs work. 452 fns now pass their own declared row -> tighter evidence
threading (469685 -> 453508 lines): m2 != m3, m3 == m4 self-confirmed; boot
re-pinned, IDE re-packed. Residue: ~146 (85 mismatch + 61 purity) is the
interning-ultimate (EffName-is-a-handle), the parameterized by-name
conflation, and the purity path.

mentl/ccb937b:
wat_to_string's `wat_emit(s) => resume() with buf = buf |> str_concat(s)`
was drift-11 at the handler-state layer — O(B^2) byte-copying per yield as
buf grew. For 1965-fn wheel emission with ~100k cumulative yields and 4MB
total output, aggregate bump-allocator pressure exhausted memory mid-pass.

ULTIMATE FORM per the eight interrogations: per-yield work O(1) amortized
(list_extend_to + list_set, doubling-buffer-counter substrate); per-result
materialization O(B+N) one-time via new str_concat_all primitive.

Two changes:
1. lib/runtime/strings.mn — add str_concat_all(xs): pass 1 sums byte_lens,
   pass 2 allocs once + memcpys each via view_base. View-substrate aware.
   Two helpers (sum_byte_lens, copy_strings_to) — tail-recursive walks.

2. src/backends/wasm.mn — wat_to_string switches to (buf = make_list, count = 0):
   wat_emit appends s's handle (no copy); wat_collect materializes via
   str_concat_all(slice(buf, 0, count)). Drift-11 closed structurally.

Pattern locks for every accumulator handler in the wheel. Per-yield
amortized O(1) is THE substrate Mentl deserves; no narrower form exists.

Verification: pass2 grows by 3 fns (str_concat_all + 2 helpers), still
validates clean. pass3 trap moved from wat_to_string OOB → lower-time
OOB at 920MB (distinct gate, distinct layer).

mentl/ccb9879:
The HM checker doesn't instantiate user-defined generic functions
(only builtins with negative TVars get fresh type vars at each call
site). memory.lux's `fn slice(list, start, end)` is user-defined,
so all call sites share the same type variable for the first param.

The prelude's starts_with, ends_with, index_of, replace, and trim
were calling `slice(s, ...)` on strings. This unified slice's shared
type variable with TString. Every subsequent call site — including
env_lookup's `slice(env, 1, len(env))` on a list of tuples — then
saw its first arg as TString. The WASM lowerer dispatched to
str_slice (byte-level) instead of slice (element-level), producing
corrupted pointers and a crash in env_lookup during check_program.

Fix: prelude string functions now use str_slice directly. This keeps
slice's type variable list-only, eliminating the cross-contamination.

Impact: 7 previously-failing golden tests now pass. The type
contamination wasn't WASM-specific — it corrupted the HM env in the
bare path too, causing wrong teaching output, incorrect did-you-mean
suggestions, and function dispatch errors.

Also adds has_tvars/has_tvars_list to ty.lux (reserved for future
let-generalization) and documents the instantiation gap in
needs_instantiation's comment.

two-top/ccadd9a:
Adds the sim/render boundary primitives so the visual layer can run at
any frame rate while the sim stays at deterministic 60 Hz. The contract:
sim writes PositionF; the first GgrsSchedule system snapshots it into
PreviousPositionF; the render layer's sync_transforms_from_sim lerps
between them weighted by how far into the current sim tick we are.

sim (crates/sim/src/lib.rs):
  * PreviousPositionF(Vec2F) component + rollback + checksum registration.
    Checksumming the snapshot too because a desync there shows up as
    visual stutter even when the live position recovers.
  * snapshot_previous system, chained FIRST in GgrsSchedule before
    player_movement.
  * NoInterpolate marker (rolled back so its presence/absence stays
    consistent during resimulation) — render-side opt-out for entities
    whose sim position changes shouldn't smear on screen.
  * snap_position(pos, prev, new) helper for teleports: collapses prev
    and pos to the same target so the lerp emits no motion.
  * AngleF / PreviousAngleF deferred to Phase 9 — Phase 7's exit
    criterion is smooth position interpolation; rotation has no
    consumer until walls/dash land.

render (new crate):
  * lerp_position(prev, curr, alpha) — pure f32 interpolation, alpha
    clamped [0, 1]. Returns Vec2 ready for Transform.translation.
  * interpolation_alpha(now, last_tick, tick_hz) — pure helper.
  * sync_transforms_from_sim — Update-schedule system; reads
    PositionF/PreviousPositionF/Option<NoInterpolate>/Time<Real>/
    LastSimTickTime, writes Transform.translation. NoInterpolate
    entities use raw current position.
  * RenderSyncPlugin wraps the system.
  * 8 unit tests on the pure helpers (alpha boundaries, clamping,
    midpoint).

run ordering, and make the planted-pattern corpus the first thing run.
